MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What number is the Roman numeral V? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 6
   C. 4
   D. 5

2. Which number is written in words as "two thousand and ninety"? (1 mark)
   A. 20,900
   B. 2,900
   C. 290
   D. 2,090

3. What is the total value of the digit 8 in 4,835? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 80
   C. 800
   D. 8,000

4. Which number is written in words as "eight thousand, two hundred and six"? (1 mark)
   A. 8,206
   B. 8,026
   C. 826
   D. 82,006

5. Which number must be added to 1,500 to make 6,000? (1 mark)
   A. 4,500
   B. 7,500
   C. 4,490
   D. 4,600

6. What is the sum when you add 1 to 9,999? (1 mark)
   A. 10,000
   B. 9,000
   C. 99,999
   D. 10,001

7. Work out 4,750 + 3,895. (1 mark)
   A. 7,545
   B. 8,655
   C. 8,545
   D. 8,645

8. Which number must be added to 2,318 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 3,425
   B. 3,415
   C. 3,525
   D. 8,061

9. What is 7 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 107
   C. 700
   D. 70

10. What is 45 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 90
   C. 65
   D. 9,000

11. What is 800 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 80
   B. 800
   C. 9
   D. 8

12. Change 2 1/3 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3/3
   B. 6/3
   C. 7/3
   D. 8/3

13. Which fraction of an hour is 30 minutes? (1 mark)
   A. 3/4
   B. 1/3
   C. 1/2
   D. 1/4

14. Change 13/3 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/3
   B. 4 1/3
   C. 4 2/3
   D. 1 4/3

15. Ali writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 1 3/4
   B. 8/3
   C. 3/8
   D. 7/4

16. In the number 9.27, the digit 7 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tenths
   B. Ones
   C. Hundredths
   D. Tens

17. Which price is the cheapest: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8.25
   B. Ksh 8.05
   C. Ksh 7.99
   D. Ksh 8.50

18. How many hundredths make one tenth? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 1
   C. 5
   D. 10

19. In the number 26.91, the digit 2 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Hundredths
   C. Tens
   D. Tenths

20. Simplify a + a + a. (1 mark)
   A. 3a
   B. 3
   C. a3
   D. a + 3

21. A rope 7 m 20 cm long is cut into 6 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 1 m 30 cm
   B. 7 m 14 cm
   C. 2 m 40 cm
   D. 1 m 20 cm

22. A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 26 cm
   B. 24 cm
   C. 25 cm
   D. 30 cm

23. What is the perimeter of a shape? (1 mark)
   A. The distance all the way round its edge
   B. The number of its corners
   C. Its longest side
   D. The space inside it

24. A square has sides of 25 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 75 m
   B. 625 m
   C. 50 m
   D. 100 m

25. A square is covered with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 12 square units
   B. 36 square units
   C. 42 square units
   D. 24 square units

26. A square is covered with 3 rows of 3 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 12 square units
   B. 9 square units
   C. 6 square units
   D. 8 square units

27. How many days are in 5 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 120 days
   B. 42 days
   C. 35 days
   D. 25 days

28. How many hours are in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 168 hours
   B. 192 hours
   C. 84 hours
   D. 420 hours

29. When is a shadow shortest? (1 mark)
   A. Around midday
   B. At night
   C. Early in the morning
   D. Late in the afternoon

30. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 6 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 7:30
   B. 6:45
   C. 6:30
   D. 6:06

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A bus leaves at 10:30 a.m. and arrives at 2:15 p.m. How long is the journey? (3 marks)

32. Explain the difference between a factor and a multiple, using the number 6 as an example. (3 marks)

33. How many right angles does a rectangle have? Explain. (2 marks)

34. What number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? Explain how you found it. (3 marks)

35. Give two things you should do to stay safe when you collect data about vehicles. (2 marks)

36. Amina faces south. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise, then a half turn, then a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face at the end? Show each step. (5 marks)

37. A mother buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

38. Add 2 hours 45 minutes and 1 hour 30 minutes. (3 marks)

39. A shopping list has 3 packets of rice at Ksh 130 each, 2 bottles of oil at Ksh 250 each and 1 tin of tomatoes at Ksh 60. Find the total cost. (4 marks)

40. Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she study in all? (3 marks)

41. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes, and change 35 days to weeks. (3 marks)

42. Write instructions for a person to walk from the classroom door to the school gate using at least two turns. Use words such as forward, quarter turn, clockwise and anticlockwise. (4 marks)

43. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers does it have? (2 marks)

44. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres, and then to metres using a decimal. (3 marks)

45. A ribbon is 5 m 20 cm long. A piece 2 m 75 cm long is cut off. How much ribbon is left? (3 marks)

46. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact answer. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 5
   V stands for 5.

2. D — 2,090
   two thousand and ninety: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 2,090.

3. C — 800
   The digit 8 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 8 × 100 = 800.

4. A — 8,206
   eight thousand, two hundred and six: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 8,206.

5. A — 4,500
   6,000 − 1,500 = 4,500. Check: 1,500 + 4,500 = 6,000.

6. A — 10,000
   9,999 + 1 = 10,000. Each 9 turns into 0 and a 1 is carried to a new place.

7. D — 8,645
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 4,750 + 3,895 = 8,645.

8. A — 3,425
   5,743 − 2,318 = 3,425. Check: 2,318 + 3,425 = 5,743.

9. C — 700
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 7 × 100 = 700.

10. A — 900
   45 × 2 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

11. D — 8
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 800 ÷ 100 = 8.

12. C — 7/3
   2 × 3 = 6 and 6 + 1 = 7. The denominator stays 3, so the answer is 7/3.

13. C — 1/2
   There are 60 minutes in an hour. 30 minutes is half of 60, so it is 1/2 of an hour.

14. B — 4 1/3
   13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. The whole number is 4 and the fraction is 1/3, so 13/3 = 4 1/3.

15. A — 1 3/4
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 1 3/4.

16. C — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 9.27 the digit 7 is in the hundredths place.

17. C — Ksh 7.99
   Compare the shillings first. 7 is less than 8, so Ksh 7.99 is the smallest.

18. D — 10
   One tenth is 10/100, so 10 hundredths make 1 tenth.

19. C — Tens
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 26.91 the digit 2 is in the tens place.

20. A — 3a
   Only like terms can be joined. a + a + a = 3a.

21. D — 1 m 20 cm
   720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm.

22. B — 24 cm
   Add all three sides: 7 + 8 + 9 = 24 cm.

23. A — The distance all the way round its edge
   Perimeter is the total length of all the sides.

24. D — 100 m
   A square has four equal sides. 25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = 100.

25. B — 36 square units
   Area = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.

26. B — 9 square units
   Area = 3 × 3 = 9 square units.

27. C — 35 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 5 × 7 = 35 days.

28. A — 168 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 7 × 24 = 168 hours.

29. A — Around midday
   At midday the Sun is highest, so shadows are very short.

30. C — 6:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 6:30.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 2 h (1 mark); 12:30 to 2:15 p.m. is 1 h 45 min (1 mark); total 3 h 45 min (1 mark).

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: A factor divides a number exactly: the factors of 6 are 1, 2, 3 and 6. A multiple is found by multiplying: the multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and so on.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4. A rectangle has four corners and each corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 and 1 mark for the reason.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,318. Subtract 5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using subtraction, 1 mark for the working, 1 mark for the answer 2,318.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Count from a safe place inside the school gate and stay with a teacher. Do not stand in or near the road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible safety rule.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: South then a quarter turn anticlockwise gives east (2 marks). East then a half turn gives west (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Final answer north (1 mark).

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: 3/4 + 1/2 = 3/4 + 2/4 (1 mark); = 5/4 (1 mark); = 1 1/4 kg (1 mark).

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 hours 15 minutes
   Working / marking points: 45 + 30 = 75 min and 2 + 1 = 3 h (1 mark); 75 min = 1 h 15 min (1 mark); total 4 h 15 min (1 mark).

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 950
   Working / marking points: 3 × 130 = 390 (1 mark); 2 × 250 = 500 (1 mark); 390 + 500 + 60 (1 mark); Ksh 950 (1 mark).

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 5 minutes
   Working / marking points: 20 + 45 = 65 min (1 mark); 1 h + 65 min = 2 h 5 min (2 marks).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 35 days = 5 weeks.
   Working / marking points: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 (1 mark for 2 h 30 min); 35 ÷ 7 = 5 (1 mark for 5 weeks); 1 mark for division working.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Walk forward 10 steps. Make a quarter turn clockwise. Walk forward 5 steps. Make a quarter turn anticlockwise. Walk to the gate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first move with steps, 1 mark for a turn with its size, 1 mark for the turn direction, 1 mark for clear order.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5 layers
   Working / marking points: 60 ÷ 12 = 5. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 50 cm and 2.5 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by 100, 1 mark for 2 m 50 cm, 1 mark for 2.5 m.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 45 cm
   Working / marking points: 520 − 275 = 245 cm (2 marks); 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm (1 mark).

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280. Exact: 5,287.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for 5,280, 1 mark for 5,287.
